ai.title: Fix websocket response-complete delivery on error
ai.summary: Removed setTimeout delay for response-complete signal in websocket-action.ts. Error paths now send response-complete immediately via direct sendAction call. Fixes issue where delayed signal was not received by client. Scope: backend websocket handler only.

eli5.text: When you send a message, the backend sends a 'done' signal to tell your client the response is finished. If something went wrong, that 'done' signal was being sent on a short delay, and sometimes your client never got it. Now it's sent right away, so error cases still close cleanly. This only affects the backend websocket message handling.

ai.title: knowledge.md add tsc instruction
ai.summary: Added Development workflow section to knowledge.md requiring `bun run tsc` execution and error fixing on every code change. Strengthened existing TypeScript guidance to explicitly forbid writing return types. Internal documentation update affecting agent behavior only.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to make changes to your code, it now has to run a type-checking step before finishing up. That check makes sure the code still makes sense to the system that understands how your code is built, and if anything is off, the assistant has to fix it before moving on. This affects the behind-the-scenes process the assistant follows, so you'll notice it if you ask for code changes and watch what happens afterward. It's live today for anyone using the assistant to edit internal project files.

ai.title: Whitespace-agnostic diff matching
ai.summary: Added fallback logic in `parseAndGetDiffBlocksSingleFile` to match diff blocks ignoring whitespace differences. This prevents failures when indentation or spacing changes cause exact string matches to fail. Implemented in `backend/src/generate-diffs-prompt.ts` with new test fixtures in `test/__mock-data__/whitespace/`.

eli5.text: When the assistant compares two versions of a code file to figure out what changed, it now falls back to ignoring extra spaces and indentation if an exact match fails. This means differences in how lines are spaced or indented no longer cause the comparison to break or miss the actual edits. Internal tools that depend on this comparison process are now more resilient to formatting-only changes.

ai.title: Strip markdown code fences from new file creation
ai.summary: backend/src/process-file-block.ts now strips leading ```lang and trailing ``` fences from newContent before writing new files. This prevents markdown artifacts from being saved as literal file content when the agent creates files via diff blocks. Scope limited to the backend file processing logic; no changes to CLI, Web, or Desktop surfaces.

eli5.text: When you create a new file through the assistant, it used to save extra formatting marks (like the triple backticks you see in code examples) as literal text inside the file. Now those marks are automatically cleaned up before the file is written. If you look at a newly created file, you'll notice it no longer contains stray quote marks or code symbols at the top and bottom. This only affects the backend process that handles file creation; the app's menus, buttons, and screens stay the same.

ai.title: Remove URL scraping from knowledge file context
ai.summary: getProjectFileContext now calls getExistingFiles instead of getExistingFilesWithScrapedContent. Removed getExistingFilesWithScrapedContent which appended scraped URL blocks to knowledge.md files. Only npm-app/src/project-files.ts affected. No migration needed; existing knowledge.md files remain unchanged.

eli5.text: When the assistant reviews your project files, it used to pull in content from web links listed in your notes file and add that text to the file before reading it. Now it skips the web-link content entirely and only reads what you already wrote in the notes file. If you open your project, you won't see any changes to the notes file itself, and the assistant simply won't have that extra pulled-in text available while helping you. This is live today as part of a routine internal update.

ai.title: Update manicode local installs
ai.summary: Update logic handles local installs. Detects installer and scope via environment variables and paths. Runs package manager commands matching scope. Covers npm-app update-manicode.ts.

eli5.text: When you ask the tool to update itself, it now checks whether you installed it globally on your system or just inside a specific project folder. Depending on what it finds, it runs the correct update command with or without the global flag. This means you no longer need to worry about whether the tool uses npm, yarn, pnpm, or bun, it figures out the right one and updates itself properly. The change is live today and only affects you when you run the update action.

ai.title: CLI trims input, accepts diff aliases
ai.summary: handleUserInput in npm-app/src/cli.ts trims userInput before command matching. diff handler accepts 'doff', 'dif', 'iff' alongside 'diff' and 'd'. Scope: CLI command parsing only. Trim applies globally, affecting all subsequent string comparisons.

eli5.text: You can now type a few typos like 'doff', 'dif', or 'iff' and the system still runs the same comparison view it shows when you type 'diff' or 'd'. When you type any command, the system now ignores extra spaces at the start or end of what you entered, so a stray space won't make a previously working command suddenly stop matching. People who talk to the assistant through the command line will notice that misspelled shortcuts for the diff view now connect to the same screen they expect, and that commands keep working even if they accidentally leave a space before or after the text they type. The change is live today.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.94
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.94 in npm-app/package.json. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: After updating to version 1.0.94, the AI assistant you use can now handle code diffs more reliably, even if the code has been slightly reformatted with different spacing or tabs. This means that when you work on projects where code style changes frequently, the assistant will still correctly understand and apply edits without confusion. The version label itself was just bumped in the background, the real improvements are in how it processes your requests.
